memo.verdict: A six-story mixed-use building with 15 to 16 units is realistically achievable under an existing site plan approval, but the project is not worth pursuing at the $475,000 asking price.
memo.as_of_right: Under CD-5 Urban Center rules (Table 345.405.A-6), maximum height is 6 stories with 100% maximum impervious lot coverage and no FAR limit. On a 2,235 square foot lot (or 2,151 square feet listed), 6 stories yield 13,410 gross square feet. Deducting ground-floor commercial space leaves 5 residential floors of 11,175 gross square feet, allowing 15 to 16 units of roughly 700 square feet each.
memo.approval_path: Existing approval. The site has an approved site plan granted April 25, 2022 for a 6-story mixed-use project, extended through April 25, 2027 by Local Law I-14 of 2025. Time and entitlement risk are low if built as approved, but plan modifications would require Planning Commission review.
legal_issues: Approval extensions and approved unit counts (15 vs 16 units) must be verified in writing with the Village.
Mandatory 10% Affordable AFFH unit set-aside is required per Section 345-405.U at 60% AMI for 50 years.
Buyer must pay unspecified additional in-lieu parking fees and GEIS fair share mitigation payments.
Property is located in FEMA Flood Zone AE, requiring floodplain code compliance and flood insurance.
memo.test_fit: The building envelope is limited first by the small lot footprint (2,235 sq ft) and the 6-story height ceiling. Setbacks (0 ft min front/side) do not shrink the building footprint. Density caps at 15 to 16 units (approved layout: 10 1-BR, 5 studio). Zero on-site spaces are provided, relying on parking reductions or a buy-out of up to $30,000 per space.
memo.value: At the $475,000 ask, land cost is $31,667 per approved unit. A second analyst's pro forma (underwriting_muse) estimates hard costs at $450 per square foot and total development costs at $7,543,125, yielding a 4.24% yield on cost at zero land value and a maximum supportable land value of negative $2,618,510.
diligence: Verify exact approved unit count and stamped site plans (15 units in offering memo vs 16 units in AKRF review).
Confirm the written status of the approval extension through April 25, 2027 with the Village of Port Chester.
Determine the exact dollar amounts for mandatory in-lieu parking fees and GEIS fair share mitigation payments.
Obtain an elevation certificate and review FEMA Zone AE flood insurance requirements.
Order a boundary survey to resolve lot area discrepancy between the tax roll (2,235 sq ft) and listing (2,151 sq ft).

independent_check.enablers: 12+ units: no - caps at 1 because 3500 sf of lot area per dwelling unit and 0.40 FAR on a 6772 sf lot. Market-rate track: no affordability mandate applies at 1 unit (331-152 triggers above 2 units); conventional product is a small one-family home of about 2709 sf FAR envelope; exit context - New Rochelle new-build asking rents at The Alary (2025): studio $2548, 1BR $3000, 2BR $4400. Affordable track: 331-152 bonus floor area (150% of affordable floor area) does not lift the 3500 sf per-unit density cap, so no added units as-of-right; a 3-4 unit project (variance or rezoning) would trigger the 10% at 70% AMI set-aside and could use NY HCR, Westchester County or federal LIHTC programs. Rezoning plausible - adjacent RMF-1.0 district (FAR 1.0) in the GIS zoning envelope, plus R2-7.0 and C-1 nearby; no comprehensive-plan direction or pending rezoning found. deal type: either - market-rate as-of-right (1 unit) or affordable-program candidate if a variance or rezoning delivers 3 or more units (NY HCR / Westchester County / LIHTC)
independent_check.max_units_estimate: HEADLINE ~1 unit - one-family home on a substandard lot of record (331-13C); existing legal 3-family disregarded as-if-vacant. Envelope: FAR cap 0.40 x 6772 = 2709 sf gross floor area; footprint cap 6772 x 30% = 2032 sf; setback envelope (35-8-8) x (186-20-30) = 19 x 136 = 2584 sf, so coverage governs footprint; gross 2032 x 3 stories = 6096 sf but FAR governs at 2709 sf. (1) Multifamily/townhouse redevelopment: 1 unit - 331-38 allows multifamily up to 4 units per lot, but density caps it: 6772 / 3500 = 1.93, so 1 unit as-of-right; 2 units need a 7000 sf lot and 70 ft width (lot is 6772 sf / 35 ft) and would need area/width variances. (2) Subdivision: 0 new lots - 6772 / 7000 is under 1 lot. (3) Second home/added unit: 0 as-of-right - a second unit needs the variance path above; 331-13C allows a one-family dwelling on a smaller lot of record if its four conditions are met. Parking: 1 unit needs 1.25/unit plus 0.25/bedroom (about 2 spaces for a 3BR) - fits. 12+ units: no - caps at 1 because 3500 sf per dwelling unit and 0.40 FAR on a 6772 sf lot. Rezoning scenario: ~4 units (basis: adjacent RMF-1.0 district with FAR 1.0 would lift the FAR cap to 6772 sf gross floor area, about 4 units at 1600 sf per dwelling unit - indicative only, the RMF-1.0 per-unit area and unit cap were not verified).

memo.verdict: As-of-right ground-up development allows only 1 single-family home of 2,709 square feet, making ground-up redevelopment unviable at the $760,000 asking price unless the existing legal 3-family structure is renovated or granted variances.
memo.as_of_right: Under RMF-0.4 district rules (331-38 and 331-29B), ground-up construction is capped at 1 single-family dwelling under section 331-13C for substandard lots. The 6,772 sf lot fails the 7,000 sf minimum lot area and 35 ft frontage fails the 70 ft minimum width. Density rules requiring 3,500 sf per dwelling unit yield 1.93 units, rounding down to 1 unit. FAR of 0.40 allows up to 2,709 sf of gross floor area. Existing 3-family density is legal nonconforming and is disregarded as-if-vacant for new build calculations.
memo.approval_path: As-of-right for 1 single-family home involving standard administrative site review with low risk and short timing. Seeking 2 to 4 units requires area and width variances or a rezoning to RMF-1.0, which carries high discretionary risk and extended public hearing timelines.
legal_issues: Substandard lot exception under 331-13C requires verifying deed date, yard setbacks, single ownership, and filed plat.
Existing 3-family structure is legal nonconforming and its density is lost if the building is demolished.
Developing 2 to 4 units requires area and lot width variances or an RMF-1.0 rezoning.
Projects creating more than 2 dwelling units trigger the Section 331-152 mandatory affordable set-aside of 10% of units at 70% AMI.
memo.test_fit: FAR of 0.40 limits maximum gross floor area to 2,709 sf, which limits density first. Maximum building coverage of 30% allows a footprint up to 2,032 sf across 3 stories (up to 35 ft height). Setback envelope is 2,584 sf (19 ft by 136 ft). As-of-right yield is 1 unit requiring about 2 parking spaces (1.25 per unit plus 0.25 per bedroom). A rezoning to RMF-1.0 could allow up to 4 units averaging 1,600 sf.
memo.value: At the $760,000 ask, land cost is $760,000 per unit ($280.55 per buildable sf) for the 1-unit as-of-right ground-up scenario. Under the existing legal 3-family configuration, land cost is $253,333 per unit. In a 4-unit rezoning scenario, land cost drops to $190,000 per unit.
diligence: Verify listing lot details, zoning, and active listing status with the listing broker.
Verify four Section 331-13C compliance conditions: deed date, yard setbacks, historical ownership, and filed plat.
Inspect the existing 3-family structure to assess repair costs versus teardown value.
Review city records to confirm the legal nonconforming status and certificates of occupancy for the 3-family use.
Check parking requirements and CPA1 status under Section 331-126.
memo.enablers: Density could be increased through area and width variances for 2 units, a rezoning to the adjacent RMF-1.0 district allowing 4 units at 1.0 FAR, or by using Section 331-152 affordable housing floor area bonuses (150% of affordable floor area) if 3 or more units are approved.
memo.highest_and_best_use: Renovation and retention of the existing legal 3-family building is the highest and best use. Ground-up construction allows only 1 single-family home as-of-right, whereas retaining the existing structure preserves 3 three-bedroom units. New-build rentals in New Rochelle command up to $2,548 for studios, $3,000 for 1BRs, and $4,400 for 2BRs at The Alary (2025). Feasibility depends on total repair costs relative to building new.

memo.highest_and_best_use: Not enough data. FACTS lack complete rental and sales comps to confirm highest and best use, though the second analyst identifies conventional market-rate rental as performing better than the affordable program track.
memo.letter_angle: Approach owner Seventy West Realty LLC directly to explore an off-market acquisition or partnership around the MX-8 zoning potential.

method:
BOUNTY feasibility memos: land-use attorney + architect review for every listed site
and the strongest off-market targets.

Two layers, kept separate on purpose:
  1. FACTS AND MATH (deterministic): parcel data from the official GIS (NYC MapPLUTO,
     Westchester County parcels), street frontage measured edge by edge, the zoning
     district's floor area (NYC ZR 23-22 standard and UAP), verified municipal rules
     (Yonkers Table 43-3 / 43-4: FAR, lot area per unit, coverage, parking), approvals
     with their public sources (bounty/data/feasibility_sites.json).
  2. MEMO (Gemini, free tier, no web access): writes the attorney/architect memo from
     those facts only. It may not add approvals, dates, numbers or programs that are not
     in the facts; anything missing is listed as a diligence item.

Output: bounty/data/feasibility.json
